Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Prakash Singh Kushwaha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. This application under section 528 Bnss has been preferred to quash the impugned charge-sheet
no. 86 of 2024 dated 07.03.2024 as well as summoning/cognizance order dated 05.09.2024
including the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 17776 of 2024 (State vs. Ankur @
Madhusudan) arising out of Case Crime No. 535 of 2023, under sections 420, 384 I.P.C. and section
66-D of I.T., Police Station-Etmaddaula, District-Agra, pending in the Court of learned Additional
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 8, Agra as well as to stay the further proceedings of
abovementioned case.

entities.text: Ankur Alias Madhusudan Alias ... vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that he is not pressing the
application on merits and confined his prayer only to the extent that the present application may be
disposed of finally with a direction to the court concerned that in case applicant surrenders before it
and applies for bail, his bail application may be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance
with law, including the law laid down in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of
Investigation and another (2022 Scc OnLine Sc 825) to which learned counsel for the respondents
have no objection.

entities.text:
Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of
Investigation and another (2022 Scc OnLine Sc 825)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4.  In view of the aforesaid, the instant application under section 528 BNSS is finally disposed of with a direction to the court concerned that in case, the applicant surrenders before the court concerned within a period of three weeks from today and applies for bail, his bail application shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with settled law.
5. However, it is made clear that till three weeks from today, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant herein.
